purpose: Validate the existing island-pollination mechanism stack against multiple admitted propagation states without making Campanula microdonta, Issue #91, or any single focal taxon a programme-wide blocker.

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: physical access failure -> directional pollen transfer -> morph-specific fruit asymmetry
signed functional mismatch -> contact/robbing/resource change -> high reproductive performance
common-ish matching decline -> divergent pollen and floral responses
qualitative_validation_targets.role: branching case; Campanula is not the only lineage
qualitative_validation_targets.do_not_require: direct Issue #91 field dependency to retain the observed multi-taxon branching pattern

qualitative_validation_targets.observed_chain: frozen signed-position prediction -> observed selection direction opposite or nonconcordant
island selfing/corolla difference without detected current island service deficit
large visitor-assemblage contrast -> similar breeding-system index despite negligible autogamy

validation_question: Can one frozen mechanism architecture generate or accommodate the observed diversity of propagation states across independent island systems without parameter tuning to any one focal taxon?
success_is: the mechanism can generate propagation, buffering and branching under predeclared state differences
no single system-specific parameter rescue is required
new systems can be added when source-native discriminator data exist
next_gate: build a multi-system qualitative validation harness around the existing ABM outputs and admitted propagation matrix, then test whether the frozen mechanism architecture covers the observed state classes without Campanula-specific tuning
claim_boundary: This registry defines qualitative validation targets only. It is not a pooled effect-size model, does not convert heterogeneous estimands into one coefficient, and does not claim that the ABM mechanism is empirically identified merely because it can reproduce a state class.
